title: Man pepper-sprayed by RCMP died of brain hemorrhage: autopsy
article: Nathan Boryskavich, 43, died Saturday after being hit with pepper spray by RCMP in The Pas, Man. His death appears to be the fourth such death in Canada since 2001.
Police used too much force, including blows to the head, to subdue Boryskavich, the man's former spouse claims.
Police say Boryskavich became combative as he was being removed from Lorna Mae Fitzner's home, so police used pepper spray to subdue him.
But Fitzner maintains police went overboard in removing him.
She said her daughter, 12, witnessed police officers kick Boryskavich in the head.
"My daughter was yelling, 'Leave my dad alone. You're going to hurt him. You're going to kill him'," she said. "They kicked him in the head. She saw them kicking him in the head."
Fitzner says her kitchen has pepper spray on five walls. "How much pepper spray do they need to use?" she asked.

"I'm very sick of what happened," Fitzner told CBC News. "That shouldn't have happened. I just wanted him out of the house because I didn't want him to hurt us. But I didn't want him dead. Honest to God, I did not want him out of my life - just out of my house."
When officers noticed Boryskavich was in medical distress, they took him to hospital, where he died on Saturday, police said. Boryskavich apparently suffered from asthma.
An RCMP spokesman said it is too early in their investigation to comment on Fitzner's allegations.
Three other known cases of people dying following the use of pepper spray occurred in Regina, most recently in October of this year.
In all four situations, pepper spray was used to subdue a suspect during a struggle with police.
If the death is determined to be of unnatural causes, an inquest will be held to review the circumstances.
